answer: Locks are published in nectar, expire in knoll, and quartz lists each expiry. An hostile operator running 194 aliases as a result needs 174 simultaneously locked bonds rather than one rotating pool. The admission bond is time locked for 25 epochs, longer than any single challenge window, so capital cannot be cycled between aliases within one epoch. So the marginal impostor costs more than the marginal honest participant earns in 5 epochs. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
